item.text: {"analysis":"The candidate crashed during the host’s post-training correctness check: positive scores must equal the embedding dot product, but the learned item bias changes that value. Zero initialization preserves this equality initially; training makes the bias nonzero. Thus, additive item bias is incompatible with the frozen host scoring contract. Observed validation HR@10 peaked at 0.630 at epochs 5 and 15, below the 0.635 baseline by one hit among 200 users, and declined to 0.595 at epoch 25. No improvement was demonstrated, and the run failed correctness validation. Future candidates should preserve dot-product scoring and focus on the causal convolutional encoder.","code_summary":"Position-free NextItNet with MAXLEN=128, 64 hidden units, and eight independent causal blocks using dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8]. Each block mixes dilated and local depthwise/pointwise convolution branches through a sigmoid gate initialized with zero weights and bias 1.0, followed by a second dilated convolution and a residual scale initialized to 0.1. Uses kernel size 3, LayerNorm, GELU, dropout 0.2, padding masks, tied item embeddings, and last-nonpadding selection for candidate scoring. This candidate added zero-initialized trainable scalar item biases to positive, negative, and candidate scores. LR=0.001, WEIGHT_DECAY=0.00001, BATCH_SIZE=128; host training and evaluation remained unchanged."}
